vpn.editFromFile: This VPN came from a file: delete it and import the new file.
vpn.editWhileOn: Turn the VPN off before editing it.
vpn.fortiSsoRefused: The VPN server didn't accept the sign-in. Connect again and sign in on the organization's page.
vpn.clientCertPair: A client certificate needs both the certificate and its private key.
vpn.fortiClientCert: The client certificate or its key couldn't be used. Check the key password, and that the key belongs to the certificate.
vm.noKvm: This computer offers no hardware virtualization
vm.noKvmGroup: This system has no kvm group for hardware virtualization
vm.groupFailed: Your account could not be added to the kvm group
vm.listFailed: The list of images couldn't be downloaded: {reason}
vm.notListed: That image isn't in its maker's list
vm.imageBusy: That image is already being downloaded
vm.hashMismatch: The download's SHA-256 isn't the one its maker lists: it was thrown away
vm.listUnsigned: {name} isn't signed by its maker, so its hashes can't be trusted: refused
vm.listBadSignature: The signature on {name} doesn't verify with its maker's pinned key ({reason}): refused
vm.imageInUse: A running machine has that image in its CD drive: shut it down first
termconf.badPath: That isn’t a valid place for the Terminal’s configuration (an absolute .json file in your home folder or on a mounted disk)
termconf.missing: The Terminal’s configuration file isn’t there
termconf.unavailable: its folder isn’t there: a disk that isn’t mounted, or a folder that was moved or renamed
termconf.denied: no permission to read or write it
termconf.notRegular: it isn’t a plain file (a link or a folder)
termconf.tooLarge: the file is too large (over 4 MB)
termconf.exists: the Terminal’s configuration file already exists
termconf.backupFailed: settings.json couldn’t be backed up, so nothing was moved
termconf.verifyFailed: the new file didn’t read back the same, so nothing was moved
termconf.corrupt: the file isn’t valid JSON for the Terminal
termconf.newer: the file was written by a newer LordOS
vm.shareProtected: A folder shared with write access can’t be, or hold, a protected file of this computer (such as the Terminal’s configuration or settings.json): the machine could change what this computer runs. Share it read-only, or share a folder without it.
